answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust: influence grows as account age times honest epochs, so new identities like mesa, falcon, or vertex start near zero and stay capped regardless of capital. An attacker splitting stake across N clones gains nothing, since each fake must grind months of honest work before swaying anything, and one detected dishonest epoch slashes its accumulated trust to zero. Attack cost is endless waiting plus permanent reset risk, making one long-lived honest identity strictly better than mass fabrication.
